rows.name: Startup conditions between processes
rows.offer: A process can wait for another to start, finish, finish cleanly, turn healthy or print a ready log line.

flisk.reason: Flisk waits for a dependency to be ready (health URL, port or running) but has no wait-for-completion condition for native one-shot jobs.

text.contains: Ready means the health URL answers

rows.name: Wait for a ready log line
rows.offer: A dependency counts as ready once a chosen regex matches a line in its output, useful for services with no health endpoint.

flisk.reason: Workers and databases without an HTTP endpoint are common in agent stacks, and Flisk's native readiness only has URL, port or alive-after-a-second.

rows.acceptance: A readyLogLine field in service.json documented in docs/service-json.md and docs/run-without-docker.md, exercised by a native-runtime test under cli/src and checked by flisk up --dry-run.

ice.basis: Impact 5: helps non-HTTP workers; confidence 6: one clear doc page; ease 5: the native readiness wait exists but log tailing must be added to it.

rows.name: Exec and HTTP health probes
rows.offer: Liveness and readiness probes run a command or an HTTP request on a period, with delay, timeout and failure threshold.

flisk.reason: Flisk checks an HTTP path (and port) before dependents start, but has no command probe, tunable period or failure threshold.

rows.name: Restart policies with backoff
rows.offer: Each process has a restart policy (never, on failure, always) with a backoff delay and a restart cap.

flisk.reason: Flisk restarts native processes with doubling backoff and gives up after quick repeated exits, but the only setting is restart: no.

text.contains: After five quick exits in a row Flisk stops restarting it
`"no"` turns off the restart on exit

rows.name: Replicas of one process
rows.offer: A process can run several instances, each told its replica number, and be scaled while running.

flisk.reason: Flisk runs 1 to 10 container replicas behind Traefik, but native processes have no replicas and no live scale command.

rows.name: Namespaces to start groups
rows.offer: Processes are grouped into namespaces that can be started, stopped or restarted together.

rows.name: Ordered and custom shutdown
rows.offer: Shutdown can run a custom command or signal per process and stop processes in reverse dependency order.

flisk.reason: flisk down stops dependents first and frees the ports, but a service cannot set its own stop command or signal.

text.contains: Stops every service, dependents first, and frees the ports.

rows.name: Env files, expansion and templating
rows.offer: Environment values expand from .env files, env_file entries, command output and Go templates.

flisk.reason: Flisk expands ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} from the project .env or shell and accepts --env-file, but has no per-service env file, command-output vars or templates.

rows.name: Override files and extends
rows.offer: Several config files merge in order, with an automatic override file and extends at file and process level.

flisk.reason: Teams with dev and CI variants of one stack need small per-environment changes, and today Flisk has one service.json per service with no layering.

rows.acceptance: A documented service.override.json or environment layer in docs/service-json.md, shown by flisk config explain and covered by a discovery test under runtime/discovery.

ice.basis: Impact 4: useful but compose-style overrides are not the launch audience's first ask; confidence 5: Flisk's own discovery model differs; ease 3: touches the Starlark discovery registry and schema.

rows.name: Strict config validation
rows.offer: A strict mode rejects unknown keys and typos at startup, and a dry run validates the file.

text.contains: Shows the services, their commands and the start order.
must be a path such as /health

rows.name: Interactive terminal UI
rows.offer: A terminal screen lists processes with state, live logs, start/stop/restart keys, scaling and a command palette.

flisk.reason: The maintainers' own comparison says local processes have no terminal UI yet, and it would show state and logs without flipping between commands.

rows.acceptance: A flisk ui screen for native runs, proven by cli/src/commands/ui.tsx handling a native project and a component test under cli/src/commands/__tests__.

ice.basis: Impact 6: the most visible gap against process-compose users; confidence 7: Flisk's own docs admit it; ease 3: cli/src/commands/ui.tsx exists but is built around the Docker and Tilt status.

rows.name: TUI themes and shortcuts
rows.offer: The terminal UI has selectable themes and remappable key bindings stored in user config files.

flisk.reason: Cosmetic customization of a UI Flisk does not yet have; revisit only after a native terminal UI exists.

rows.name: Interactive processes with a PTY
rows.offer: A process can get a pseudo-terminal so you can type into REPLs and debuggers from the TUI, or send keys remotely.

flisk.reason: Flisk services run as non-interactive, logged processes for agents and CI; REPLs and debuggers belong in the user's own terminal.

rows.name: Watch files and restart
rows.offer: A process restarts when watched files change, with include/exclude globs, debounce and optional restart of dependents.

flisk.reason: Container services get file sync and live reload through Tilt, but native command services are not restarted when files change.

rows.name: Cron and interval jobs
rows.offer: A process can run on a cron expression or fixed interval with overlap control.

flisk.reason: Flisk is a dev inner loop for services and agents; recurring jobs belong in the app's own scheduler or in production tooling.

rows.name: REST API with OpenAPI
rows.offer: A running instance serves a REST and WebSocket API to list, start, stop, restart and monitor processes.

flisk.reason: Flisk exposes its state through the CLI with --json and the MCP server rather than a long-running HTTP daemon.

rows.name: API token and unix socket
rows.offer: The control API can require a token header or listen only on a local unix socket.

flisk.reason: There is no Flisk HTTP control server to protect; the MCP server runs over local stdio.

rows.name: MCP server for AI assistants
rows.offer: An MCP server over stdio or SSE lets assistants start, stop, restart and inspect processes and read logs.

rows.name: Commands exposed as MCP tools
rows.offer: A process with an mcp block becomes an MCP tool with typed arguments or a resource, run on demand.

flisk.reason: Flisk's agent surface is its own fixed tool set plus an mcp resource type for running real MCP servers; wrapping arbitrary shell commands as tools is a different product.

rows.name: Search logs from the agent
rows.offer: The assistant can fetch, truncate or search a process's logs, with relevance ranking.

flisk.reason: Agents debugging a failing service read bounded snapshots today and must scan the lines themselves.

rows.acceptance: A search or grep input on the logs MCP tool in cli/src/mcp/tools.ts and a matching flisk logs --grep flag, covered by a test in cli/src/mcp/__tests__.

ice.basis: Impact 5: agents lose time on long logs; confidence 6: the tool is documented but ranking is optional; ease 6: buildLogsArgs and the logs command already take filters.

rows.name: Dependency graph view
rows.offer: The dependency tree can be printed as ASCII, Mermaid, JSON or YAML, and shown in the TUI and API.

flisk.reason: Flisk already builds the dependsOn graph in discovery, and showing it would help people and agents understand start order.

rows.acceptance: A flisk graph command (cli/src/commands/graph.ts) and an MCP tool, with a Mermaid output test under cli/src/commands/__tests__.

ice.basis: Impact 5: nice for onboarding and debugging order; confidence 7: the page is clear; ease 6: the DAG exists in runtime/discovery and the native start order is already computed.

rows.name: Per-process logs and rotation
rows.offer: Logs go to per-process or one unified file, with size, age and gzip rotation and formatting options.

flisk.reason: Flisk writes timestamped per-service log files and merges them in flisk logs with --tail and --since, but has no rotation or format settings.
